prerequisites: It is recommended to have studied Chemistry in high school; it is necessary to know and understand the basic concepts of general chemistry to successfully undertake this first-year course.
If this subject has not been taken, it is advisable to complete Course 0 before the start of the academic year.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply the basic principles of general, organic and inorganic chemistry to engineering.
Recognize and understand the basic principles of general, organic and inorganic chemistry that apply to engineering.
Recognize and understand the training needs that will be useful to successfully solve new situations related to industrial engineering.
Act effectively in a multilingual and multidisciplinary team.
Ability to perform laboratory setups and experiments.
Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society.
Develop professional texts and scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the field of industrial technical engineering.
Adapt the organization of content and the use of verbal and non-verbal language to argue in diverse situations or before diverse audiences.
Apply the knowledge of industrial engineering in the learning of new methods and theories.
Critically and constructively show the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem.

syllabus_topics: Block 1. States of aggregation of matter and solutions
Topic 2: States of aggregation of matter and solutions
Block 3. Acid-base, solubility equilibrium and electrochemistry
Block 5. Organic chemistry. Reactivity and applications of organic compounds
Topic 9: Structure and reactivity of organic compounds
Practical 1: Usage rules and safety measures. Use of apparatus and handling of chemical products.
Practical 3: Stoichiometry of a compound. Law of conservation of matter.
Practical 5: Electrolysis. Experimental determination of Faraday's constant
assessment_rules: Mixed tests consist of two written partial exams, each accounting for 40% of the final grade, with short-answer questions and problems. Practical cases are compulsory and must be approved to evaluate other aspects of the course. Continuous assessment includes active class attendance and participation in tutorials.
